sections.heading: When to stop the strong actives and fall back to a base routine
body: There is a moment most people miss: when skin starts stinging at something it tolerated last week. That is not a sign to add another active, it is a sign the barrier is thinning.
Other signs in the same family: tightness right after washing even with a gentle cleanser; flushing at temperature changes; a familiar moisturiser suddenly feeling slightly sharp going on.
At that point the job is to subtract, not add. Keep three steps — cleanse, moisturise, sun protection — and pause everything else until those signs have gone.

sections.heading: How to read INCI order, and why position matters more than presence
body: An INCI list runs in descending proportion down to the 1% threshold; below that the manufacturer chooses the order. So an ingredient listed fifth is certainly present in greater quantity than one listed thirtieth.
This is why “contains niacinamide” says almost nothing. A formula with niacinamide fifth and one with it thirty-eighth may both print that sentence on the box.
On this site, where the manufacturer publishes the full list we print the full list. Where the packaging shows only a few groups, we print only those groups and do not fill in the rest ourselves.

sections.heading: Extra layers do not add extra effect
body: Layering many products rests on a simple assumption: more is better. For skin that assumption fails — the amount of active that crosses the outer layer is limited, and the surplus sits on the surface.
What sits there does two unwanted things: it traps heat and sebum, and it makes sunscreen applied afterwards adhere less well.
Two moisturisers stacked on each other is the clearest case. Pick one.

faq.q: What should I use after laser or microneedling?
faq.a: That is a medical situation, and the right person to answer is the doctor who performed it. This site does not replace that advice, even where the manufacturer positions a product for that group.

faq.q: Do I have to stop the brightening cream to use a recovery one?
faq.a: If your skin shows signs of thinning — stinging, tightness, redness — pause the treatment step and keep the three basics until it settles. Two weeks off and then returning is still faster than pushing through and needing two months off.

faq.q: Can a moisturiser work as sunscreen?
faq.a: No, even where titanium dioxide or zinc oxide appear in the ingredients. Those work as filters only at high concentration in a formula designed and tested for that purpose.
